bb_the_fee_explained.description: Nizzik is putting the landing fee up on the Ratchet boat specifically, by order, with a date, and she has been told to expect the small hulls to start beaching on the sand east of the cape rather than come up the ramp and pay. They already have. Bloodsail bosuns are taking a cut off every keel that lands there, which means the dodgers are paying a worse toll to a worse collector, and Nizzik finds that funnier than she should.
bb_the_fee_explained.accept_text:
Up a silver on the Ratchet run from the first tide of next month. Not my decision and I would have made the same one. The ones dodging it are beaching on the shallows and handing the difference to a bosun with a knife, which is the market working. Go and break that up anyway. Walk the beach track while you are down there so the carters can see it being walked.

The Bloodsail Shallows are east of our gate, along the south shore.

bb_stoneshapers.accept_text:
Two silver for where to look, and you pay first, because I am eleven and not stupid. Great court, the big flat one with the steps. There is a crew in there cutting stone and one of them stands back and says a number and the rest of them cut to it. Go and stand in that court and look at the faces they are cutting, then come back, because if it is true I am selling it to the Baron and I need somebody grown to have seen it.

Zul'Kundaraz. North-east of the Bay, up in the hills, and it is a long walk even for somebody grown.

bb_landing_fee.accept_text: Landing fee. You have already landed, so we are only arguing about the amount, and I will save you the trouble: it is four silver and it has been four silver since the road closed. No coin, then work. Go back up the ramp and clear the apron. Clear them off the cart track and walk the whole apron, not the first ten yards of it. I will mark you paid when the carters stop leaving loads in the trees.

bb_oonas_name.turn_in_text: Good. Now listen, because this is what I owe you and I pay what I owe. The Bloodsail do not hold that beach. They hold the water. The camp on the sand is a lure and it is meant to be counted - that is why it is pitched where the tower can see it. Everything that matters to them is afloat and off the bars, and the Baron has been buying headcounts of a camp for three years. Sell him that. Do not give it to him.
bb_oonas_name.accept_text: There is a bosun on that beach who sold me to these people for a boat and a share. I am not going to tell you which one he is, because you will take them and one of them will be him and I will sleep. Go and walk through the camp while you are at it. And do not look at me like that. You people came in on boats that came out of the sky. Mine came out of a shipyard in Kul Tiras. We are both standing in a goblin port a long way from where we started and only one of us is in a cage, so spare me.

bb_the_third_wreck.turn_in_text: Weezel reads all of them, sets them down squarely, and lines up their edges before he says anything. Yard, year, number. Yes. That hull was written off in the week the road closed, and I signed the write-off, and it was the easiest signature of my career. A hull lost in that week was lost to the weather. A hull lost in the week before it would have been lost to me. So no. I will not be filing this. I file about a diary every week because a diary cannot be audited and I can. Keep them. Sell them to the fence if you want - he will know the year.
bb_the_third_wreck.accept_text: Low water, east bar, and the Bloodsail cannoneers will work on you the entire time you are out there, so give them something nearer to think about first. The plates are on the frames, inboard, where the barnacle has not got at them. Keep them on you. I do not want them - I have looked at that hull for three years and I know exactly what it is. Take them up the gallery, put them in Weezel's hands, and watch what his face does. That is the part I am paying for.

bb_the_salvage.accept_text: Fittings. Rings, pins, braces, anything forged. Not planking, I do not want planking, I have a jungle of planking and no pins to hold it together. Nobody gets this right the first time, so: the salvagers carry it on them, on a line, the way you would carry keys. Take them and walk the drowned courts down to where the water starts standing, and bring me back anything that rings when you drop it.

bb_tidecallers.accept_text: Six days the shoals have gone in through that mouth on a falling tide. Fish do not swim into a hole uphill. Something is calling the water in and the fish are going where the water goes. The ones doing it are in the halls, and they are not the naga, and I will not say more than that because I have not been down there and you will have. The myrmidons are in your way. The Kundaraz tidecallers are the job.
